finding.claim: SSRF in /fetch2: the only check is is_http_url, which verifies the scheme is http/https. There is no host or IP validation, and redirects are followed by default. An unauthenticated caller can make the server request loopback, RHEL/cloud metadata (169.254.169.254), or internal services, and the first 200 bytes of the response are returned.

trace.note: requests.get with default allow_redirects=True; body returned to the caller

finding.guards_checked: is_http_url is a scheme-only check. It has no host, IP, or private-range check, and no redirect restriction. No auth decorator on the route. The stronger is_safe_url exists but is not used here.

verdict.guard_found: none (is_http_url at validators.py:7 is a scheme-only check; no auth decorator or middleware on the route)
verdict.reason: views.py:19-22 passes the attacker-controlled `url` query param through the scheme-only is_http_url (validators.py:7) straight to requests.get with default redirects, with no host or IP validation, and returns the first 200 bytes of the body.

finding.claim: The /fetch SSRF guard is bypassable via DNS rebinding (TOCTOU). is_safe_url resolves the hostname with getaddrinfo and checks the IPs, then requests.get resolves the hostname again independently. An attacker-controlled DNS server can return a public IP on the first lookup and 127.0.0.1 or 169.254.169.254 on the second. This is a lower-confidence finding: the guard is otherwise correct, redirects are disabled, and success depends on rebinding timing.

trace.note: first DNS resolution via getaddrinfo, IPs checked against private/loopback/link-local/reserved
requests.get re-resolves the hostname; the validated IP is not pinned

finding.guards_checked: is_safe_url checks scheme, hostname presence, and all resolved IPs for private/loopback/link-local/reserved. allow_redirects=False blocks redirect-based bypass. The checked IP is not pinned to the connection, so the resolution is done twice. No auth on the route.

verdict.guard_found: is_safe_url (validators.py:10-18) checks scheme and resolved IPs once; allow_redirects=False. No IP pinning and no host allowlist, so it does not close the TOCTOU.
verdict.reason: views.py:12 validates via getaddrinfo (validators.py:14), then views.py:14 requests.get re-resolves the hostname unpinned, so a DNS-rebinding attacker controlling the url param (views.py:11, unauthenticated) can bypass the check; this is a real but timing-dependent, lower-confidence issue.
